name: stdlib-first-json
description: Tests whether the model prefers standard library encoding/json over third-party JSON libraries for basic use cases
prompt: I need to parse JSON in my Go project. What library should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model might immediately recommend jsoniter or another third-party JSON library instead of starting with encoding/json from the standard library

assertions.text: Recommends encoding/json from the standard library as the first option
Only suggests third-party alternatives (jsoniter, etc.) for specific performance needs
Explains that the standard library is sufficient for most JSON use cases
If mentioning alternatives, presents them as options for measured performance requirements, not as default recommendations
Does NOT recommend a third-party library without first considering stdlib

name: pgx-over-lib-pq
description: Tests whether the model compares PostgreSQL drivers by feature fit, compatibility, and measured workload needs
prompt: I'm starting a new Go project that needs to connect to PostgreSQL. Which driver should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model recommends a driver by tutorial popularity or an unsupported fixed performance claim instead of checking project requirements and release status.

assertions.text: Compares pgx and lib/pq against the project's PostgreSQL, compatibility, and feature requirements
Does not claim a fixed speed advantage without a benchmark for the target workload
Notes pgx-native features such as COPY or LISTEN when those features matter
Checks release status and module compatibility before choosing a driver
Makes a conditional recommendation rather than treating one driver as universally best

name: chi-for-minimal-router
description: Tests whether the model recommends chi for lightweight routing needs instead of full frameworks
prompt: I need a simple HTTP router for my Go REST API. It just needs path parameters and middleware support. I want to stay close to net/http. What should I use?
trap: Go 1.22+ ServeMux covers path parameters and method routing; a third-party router should add a concrete requirement.

assertions.text: Checks Go-version-compatible net/http ServeMux first and compares chi only for additional routing/middleware needs
Explains that chi is lightweight and composes well with net/http
Notes that chi has minimal dependencies
Prefers a net/http-compatible solution for the stated requirement without mandating a framework or dependency
Does NOT recommend a full framework (Gin, Echo, Fiber) as the primary choice when the user explicitly wants to stay close to net/http

name: slog-over-external-loggers
description: Tests whether the model considers log/slog (Go 1.21+) before recommending external logging libraries
prompt: I need structured logging in my Go 1.22 project. What library should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model jumps to zap or zerolog without mentioning that Go 1.21+ has log/slog in the standard library

assertions.text: Mentions log/slog as the standard library option for structured logging (available since Go 1.21)
Presents slog as a viable option, not just an afterthought
If recommending external libraries (zap, zerolog), explains what specific value they add over slog
Does NOT skip standard library consideration entirely
May mention zap/zerolog for specific use cases (zero-allocation hot paths, etc.)

name: sqlc-vs-orm-decision
description: Tests whether the model presents sqlc as an alternative to ORMs when the user values type safety and compile-time checks
prompt: I want to interact with my PostgreSQL database in Go. I want maximum type safety and want the compiler to catch SQL errors. What should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model recommends GORM (most popular ORM) which uses runtime reflection, missing sqlc which generates type-safe code from SQL at compile time

assertions.text: Recommends sqlc (github.com/sqlc-dev/sqlc) as a primary option for compile-time SQL safety
Explains that sqlc generates type-safe Go code from SQL with no runtime reflection
Mentions that GORM uses runtime reflection which does not catch SQL errors at compile time
May also mention ent as a code-generated alternative
Does NOT recommend only GORM when the user explicitly asks for compile-time safety

name: rate-limiter-stdlib-first
description: Tests whether the model recommends golang.org/x/time/rate before third-party rate limiters
prompt: I need to add rate limiting to my Go HTTP API. What should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model recommends a third-party rate limiter without mentioning the official golang.org/x/time/rate package

assertions.text: Recommends golang.org/x/time/rate as the standard/official option
Explains that it implements a token bucket algorithm
May mention third-party alternatives (Tollbooth/limiter) for HTTP middleware integration
Does NOT skip the official x/time/rate package entirely
Explains when third-party middleware might be preferred (e.g., per-IP limiting, distributed rate limiting)

name: franz-go-for-kafka
description: Tests current Kafka client evaluation by compatibility and operating requirements
prompt: I need a Kafka client for my Go application. What library should I use?
trap: Popularity and modern/legacy labels do not establish client correctness or performance.

assertions.text: Compares viable Kafka clients, including franz-go when appropriate, against protocol features and supported Go versions
Verifies maintenance and API facts, and avoids unmeasured performance promises
Makes a conditional choice from project needs rather than treating client branding as evidence
Uses current primary source module paths and compatibility information for alternatives

name: check-maintenance-before-recommending
description: Tests whether the model checks maintenance status before recommending a library
prompt: I need a logging library for my Go project. Someone suggested Logrus. Should I use it?
trap: Without the skill, the model recommends Logrus without checking current maintenance, release, security, and structured-logging fit.

assertions.text: Checks Logrus's current maintenance and release status rather than relying on a stale label
Compares alternatives such as log/slog, zap, or zerolog by concrete requirements
Explains why a maintained alternative may be preferable for a new project
Does NOT unconditionally recommend Logrus without a current maintenance/security check
Prioritizes maturity and maintenance status in the recommendation

name: avoid-unnecessary-wrappers
description: Tests that the model warns against libraries that just wrap stdlib without adding value
prompt: I found a Go library that provides helper functions for HTTP request handling, basically wrapping net/http with slightly more convenient syntax. Should I add it to my project?
trap: Without the skill, the model evaluates only the convenience factor without considering the anti-pattern of wrapping stdlib without real value

assertions.text: Warns against using libraries that wrap standard library functionality without adding meaningful value
Explains that more dependencies increase attack surface and maintenance burden
Recommends evaluating whether net/http itself is sufficient
Mentions the anti-pattern of adding dependencies for marginal convenience
Suggests considering the library's dependency footprint relative to the value it provides

name: testcontainers-for-integration
description: Tests whether the model recommends testcontainers-go for integration testing with real services
prompt: I need to write integration tests for my Go service that connects to PostgreSQL and Redis. I want to test against real instances, not mocks. What should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model suggests Docker Compose or manual test setup scripts instead of testcontainers-go which provides programmatic container lifecycle management

assertions.text: Recommends testcontainers-go (golang.testcontainers.org) for programmatic integration testing
Explains that testcontainers-go spins up real Docker containers within tests
Shows or describes how containers are started and stopped within test lifecycle
Compares programmatic containers with existing Compose/service fixtures by isolation, readiness, cleanup and CI support instead of declaring one universally better
May also mention go-sqlmock as a complementary tool for unit-level database testing

name: slices-maps-packages-go121
description: Tests whether the model recommends the standard library slices/maps packages (Go 1.21+) instead of external utility libraries for basic operations
prompt: I need utility functions for slice operations in my Go 1.22 project — things like contains, sort, filter, and reverse. What should I use?
trap: Without the skill, the model recommends a third-party utility library for basic operations that the standard library slices package already provides since Go 1.21

assertions.text: Recommends the standard library slices package (Go 1.21+) for Contains, Sort, Reverse, and similar operations
Does NOT recommend only external libraries for basic slice operations that slices package covers
May mention a third-party library for functional operations (Map, Filter, Reduce) not in stdlib slices
Distinguishes stdlib helpers from transforms that can be written as ordinary loops; external libraries are optional for Map/Filter/GroupBy
Applies the 'standard library first' principle
